governance.purpose: Regimen-specific consent discussion support. It does not replace the HSE National Consent Policy, the NCCP consent process, the current NCCP regimen or clinician judgement.
governance.patient_identifiers: SACTCheck does not request or persist patient name, MRN, DOB or other direct identifiers. Complete identifiers only in the approved clinical record or on the printed form.

sources.label: HSE National Consent Policy
sources.role: Consent must be voluntary and informed, with understandable information on treatment, benefits, risks, alternatives and what may happen if treatment does not proceed.

sources.label: NCCP SACT Guidance and Related Documents
sources.role: National SACT resources including the Systemic Anti-Cancer Therapy Patient Consent Form – Medical Oncology.

sources.label: NCCP National SACT Regimens

cytotoxic_chemotherapy.label: Generic chemotherapy consent
cytotoxic_chemotherapy.description: Common and important risks that may occur with cytotoxic chemotherapy. The exact likelihood and severity vary by regimen and patient.

risks.label: Bone-marrow suppression and infection
risks.detail: White blood cells can fall, increasing infection and neutropenic-sepsis risk. Urgent assessment may be required for fever or acute illness.

risks.label: Anaemia and fatigue
risks.detail: Red blood cells may fall and tiredness, breathlessness or reduced exercise tolerance can occur.

risks.label: Low platelets and bleeding
risks.detail: Platelet counts can fall, increasing bruising or bleeding risk.

risks.label: Nausea and vomiting
risks.detail: Anti-sickness medicines may be needed. Severity depends on the regimen.

risks.label: Diarrhoea or constipation
risks.detail: Bowel disturbance can occur and can occasionally become severe or cause dehydration.

risks.label: Mouth soreness / mucositis
risks.detail: Inflammation or ulceration of the mouth and gastrointestinal lining may occur.

risks.label: Hair, skin or nail changes
risks.detail: Hair loss or thinning and skin/nail changes may occur depending on the medicines used.

risks.label: Allergic or infusion reactions
risks.detail: Reactions can occur during or shortly after administration and can rarely be severe.

risks.label: Pregnancy, contraception and fertility
risks.detail: Some anti-cancer medicines can harm an unborn baby and may affect fertility. Discuss contraception and fertility preservation where relevant.

risks.label: Organ-specific toxicity
risks.detail: Individual drugs can affect nerves, heart, lungs, kidneys, liver, hearing or other organs. The agent-specific section below lists important regimen-specific risks.

immune_checkpoint_inhibitor.label: Generic immunotherapy consent
immune_checkpoint_inhibitor.description: Immune-checkpoint inhibitors can cause inflammatory toxicity in almost any organ. Toxicity may occur during treatment or after treatment has stopped and can occasionally be life-threatening.

risks.label: Pneumonitis
risks.detail: Immune-related lung inflammation can cause new cough, breathlessness or chest symptoms and can be life-threatening.

risks.label: Diarrhoea / colitis
risks.detail: Immune-related bowel inflammation can cause diarrhoea, abdominal pain, blood or mucus in stool and can become severe.

risks.label: Hepatitis
risks.detail: Immune-related liver inflammation can cause abnormal liver tests or jaundice and can occasionally be severe.

risks.label: Endocrine toxicity
risks.detail: Thyroid, pituitary, adrenal or pancreatic inflammation can occur; some hormone deficiencies can be permanent and require replacement.

risks.label: Nephritis
risks.detail: Immune-related kidney inflammation can impair renal function and may require immunosuppression and treatment interruption.

risks.label: Severe skin toxicity
risks.detail: Rash and itch are common; rare severe blistering or mucosal reactions require urgent assessment.

risks.label: Myocarditis / pericarditis
risks.detail: Rare immune inflammation of the heart muscle or surrounding tissues can cause chest pain, breathlessness, rhythm disturbance or heart failure and may be life-threatening.

risks.label: Neurological immune toxicity
risks.detail: Rare encephalitis, neuropathy, myasthenic syndromes or other neurological inflammation can cause confusion, seizures, weakness, sensory change or breathing difficulty.

risks.label: Myositis / neuromuscular toxicity
risks.detail: Immune-mediated muscle inflammation can cause pain, weakness or swallowing/breathing difficulty and may overlap with myocarditis or neurological toxicity.

risks.label: Ocular inflammation
risks.detail: Rare immune-related eye inflammation can cause pain, redness or visual change and requires prompt review.

risks.label: Pancreatitis / pancreatic inflammation
risks.detail: Rare pancreatic inflammation can cause abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting and may require investigation and treatment interruption.

risks.label: Infusion / administration reaction
risks.detail: Administration reactions can occur and can occasionally be severe.

risks.label: Delayed or persistent immune toxicity
risks.detail: Immune-related adverse events can begin after treatment has stopped, and some effects - particularly endocrine effects - can persist.

risks.label: Steroids / immunosuppression / hormone replacement
risks.detail: Immune toxicity may require corticosteroids or other immunosuppression, hormone replacement, hospital treatment, treatment interruption or permanent discontinuation.

risks.label: Rare life-threatening or fatal immune toxicity
risks.detail: Severe immune-related complications are uncommon but can deteriorate rapidly; new significant symptoms should be assessed promptly.

atezolizumab.source_basis: Current EMA Tecentriq product information updated 21/07/2026 and NCCP 00831 v2a pages 5–9/12. Shared immune module and existing pooled-monotherapy frequency estimates preserved; these are not HCC combination-specific incidence estimates.

risks.label: Delayed or lasting immune effects
risks.detail: Immune inflammation can affect healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Some hormone changes need long-term replacement. Carry the immunotherapy alert card and tell all treating professionals about current or previous immunotherapy.

risks.label: Infusion or subcutaneous administration reactions
risks.detail: Report breathing difficulty, swelling, rash, chest tightness or dizziness immediately. IV and thigh-injection formulations have different doses; the team confirms the prescribed formulation.

risks.label: Pregnancy prevention and breastfeeding
risks.detail: Discuss fertility and pregnancy risks. Use effective contraception during treatment and for five months after the last dose; additional combination medicines may require a longer interval. Discuss breastfeeding with the team and follow the stricter combination restriction.

immune_frequency_source.label: Tecentriq (atezolizumab) SmPC, section 4.8
immune_frequency_source.caveat: Approximate pooled monotherapy incidence; individual risk may differ by indication, combination therapy, route and patient factors.

rare_immune_events.label: Myocarditis
rare_immune_events.detail: Rare immune-mediated myocarditis, including fatal cases, has been reported.

rare_immune_events.label: Meningoencephalitis
rare_immune_events.detail: Immune-mediated meningitis or encephalitis can cause confusion, headache, seizures or neurological change.

rare_immune_events.label: Guillain-Barre / demyelinating neuropathy
rare_immune_events.detail: Rare immune-mediated demyelinating neuropathy may cause progressive weakness or sensory symptoms.

rare_immune_events.label: Myasthenia gravis / myasthenic syndrome
rare_immune_events.detail: Rare immune neuromuscular toxicity can cause weakness, swallowing difficulty or respiratory compromise.

rare_immune_events.label: Myositis
rare_immune_events.detail: Immune-mediated muscle inflammation can cause pain or weakness and may overlap with myocarditis.

rare_immune_events.label: Pancreatitis
rare_immune_events.detail: Immune-mediated pancreatic inflammation can cause abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting.

rare_immune_events.label: Pericardial disorders
rare_immune_events.detail: Immune-related pericardial inflammation or effusion can occur.

rare_immune_events.label: Ocular inflammation
rare_immune_events.detail: Rare immune-related eye inflammation can cause pain, redness or visual change.

risks.label: Myelosuppression

risks.label: Febrile neutropenia
risks.detail: Fever with neutropenia requires urgent assessment.

risks.label: Nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea
risks.detail: Gastrointestinal toxicity can occur and may cause dehydration.

risks.label: Oral schedule and tablet safety
risks.detail: Take only the prescribed morning/evening tablets on Days 1–5 and 8–12 of each authorised 28-day cycle, within one hour after meals. Tablet quantities may differ between morning and evening. Do not make up missed, held or vomited doses.

risks.label: Fatigue, poor appetite and mouth soreness
risks.detail: These can affect daily activities and nutrition; report early so treatment and support can be adjusted.

risks.label: Kidney impairment and treatment toxicity
risks.detail: Reduced kidney function can increase marrow and other toxicity, require a lower starting dose and closer blood-count monitoring. Dehydration or reduced urine needs prompt advice.

risks.label: Pregnancy, contraception and breastfeeding
risks.detail: Discuss fertility and avoid pregnancy. Women need highly effective contraception during treatment and six months afterwards, adding a barrier method to hormonal contraception. Men with partners who could become pregnant need effective contraception during treatment and six months after. Do not breastfeed during treatment.

bevacizumab.source_basis: Current EMA Avastin product information updated 27/01/2026, Tecentriq HCC precautions and NCCP 00831 v2a. HCC-specific varices information is conditional; other bevacizumab regimens retain their own context.

risks.label: Hypertension
risks.detail: Blood pressure can rise and may require treatment interruption or antihypertensive therapy.

risks.label: Proteinuria / renal injury
risks.detail: Protein loss in urine may signal kidney injury and can become severe, including nephrotic syndrome. Urine checks and sometimes a timed collection guide treatment interruption or stopping.

risks.label: Bleeding
risks.detail: Bleeding can be serious or fatal. In HCC, underlying liver disease and varices require screening and management before treatment. Black stools or vomiting blood need urgent help; other indications have their own bleeding-risk review.

risks.label: Arterial or venous thromboembolism
risks.detail: Blood clots can occur.

risks.label: Impaired wound healing
risks.detail: Treatment can impair wound healing and timing around surgery is important.

risks.label: Gastrointestinal perforation / fistula
risks.detail: Rare bowel perforation or fistula can be life-threatening.

risks.label: Jaw-bone damage (osteonecrosis of the jaw)
risks.detail: Jaw pain, swelling, a loose tooth or an unhealed mouth wound may be signs of jaw-bone damage. Tell the oncology team and dentist.

risks.label: Rare brain condition (PRES)
risks.detail: Rare serious neurological condition: headache, changes in vision, confusion or seizure, with or without high blood pressure.

risks.label: Fertility, pregnancy prevention and breastfeeding
risks.detail: Ovarian function may be affected; discuss fertility before treatment. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least six months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least six months afterwards.

risks.label: Interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis
risks.detail: Serious and sometimes fatal lung inflammation can occur. New or worsening cough, breathlessness or fever needs urgent assessment; suspected disease requires interruption and confirmed disease permanent stopping under NCCP.

risks.label: Heart rhythm changes and reduced heart function
risks.detail: QT prolongation can cause serious arrhythmias; heart pumping function can fall. Fainting, palpitations, chest pain or new breathlessness needs urgent advice. ECG and risk-based heart-function monitoring are required.

risks.label: Severe skin reactions including SJS/TEN
risks.detail: Blistering, peeling or sores involving the mouth, eyes or genitals need urgent assessment; confirmed Stevens–Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis requires permanent stopping.

risks.label: Blood-count changes and aplastic anaemia
risks.detail: Low blood counts can increase infection, bleeding or anaemia risks. Persistent fever, bruising, bleeding, pallor or marked fatigue needs assessment; confirmed aplastic anaemia requires permanent stopping.

risks.label: Rash, nail changes, diarrhoea and mouth soreness
risks.detail: These can affect daily life, eating and drinking. Report early so support can be adjusted; severe diarrhoea or dehydration needs urgent advice and treatment may need a hold or dose change.

risks.label: Eye inflammation / keratitis
risks.detail: Eye pain, redness, light sensitivity or blurred vision requires prompt ophthalmology advice.

risks.label: Pregnancy, contraception, fertility and breastfeeding
risks.detail: Avoid pregnancy; use effective contraception during treatment and for at least two months afterwards for women and four months for men. Hormonal contraceptive effectiveness may be reduced. Do not breastfeed during treatment; discuss fertility before starting.

risks.label: Medicine interactions
risks.detail: St John’s wort must not be taken with osimertinib. Strong enzyme-inducing medicines and QT-prolonging medicines need pharmacy review, including supportive medicines and supplements.

serplulimab.source_basis: NCCP00908 v1b (https://healthservice.hse.ie/documents/6856/908_NCCP_SACT_Regimen_Serplulimab.pdf), pages6–8, and EMA Hetronifly overview (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/EPAR/hetronifly), checked2026-10-26. Current EMA SmPC updated8October2026 was downloaded and sections4.2,4.4,4.8,5.1 reconciled (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/product-information/hetronifly-epar-product-information_en.pdf). These qualitative risks do not import another checkpoint inhibitor’s frequencies.

risks.label: Immune inflammation of healthy organs
risks.detail: Lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, skin, pancreas, heart, nervous system (including myasthenia and encephalitis), eyes and blood cells can be affected. Some reactions are severe or life-threatening and can occur after treatment ends.

risks.label: Hormone-gland inflammation or diabetes
risks.detail: Thyroid, pituitary or adrenal problems and type1diabetes can cause marked weakness, dizziness, headache, thirst or other symptoms. Some effects need long-term hormone replacement; severe endocrine crises need urgent care.

risks.label: Infusion reaction
risks.detail: Reactions can include flushing, itching, breathing changes or feeling faint. Tell the nurse immediately; serious reactions require stopping serplulimab.

risks.label: Severe skin reaction
risks.detail: Blistering or peeling skin and sores around the mouth or eyes need urgent assessment; some severe skin syndromes require permanent treatment discontinuation.

alectinib.source_basis: NCCP 00401 v6 pages 3–4 and EMA Alecensa SmPC updated 31 March 2026, sections 4.4–4.8. Frequency estimates are not borrowed from other ALK inhibitors.

risks.label: Liver injury
risks.detail: Raised liver tests and bilirubin can occur; liver injury may need interruption, dose reduction or stopping. Keep scheduled blood tests and report jaundice or dark urine.

risks.label: Lung inflammation (ILD / pneumonitis)
risks.detail: New cough or breathlessness needs prompt assessment. Alectinib-related lung inflammation can require permanent discontinuation.

risks.label: Muscle injury / raised CPK
risks.detail: Unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness needs review and CPK testing. Severe or recurrent elevations may require interruption and dose reduction.

risks.label: Anaemia including red-cell breakdown
risks.detail: Anaemia can include haemolysis. Report marked tiredness, pallor, breathlessness or dark urine; additional blood tests and treatment interruption may be required.

risks.label: Slow heart rate
risks.detail: Symptomatic or life-threatening bradycardia can occur. Dizziness or fainting needs urgent assessment and a review of other medicines.

risks.label: Gastrointestinal perforation
risks.detail: Perforation has been reported in patients at increased risk. Severe abdominal pain needs urgent assessment; stopping may be considered.

risks.label: Rash and sunlight sensitivity
risks.detail: Skin effects and photosensitivity can occur. Avoid prolonged sun exposure; use SPF 50 or higher sunscreen and lip balm during treatment and for at least 7 days after stopping.

risks.label: Bowel symptoms, nausea and swelling
risks.detail: Constipation, nausea, diarrhoea and swelling can affect daily activities; report persistent symptoms and poor intake.

risks.label: Pregnancy, contraception and breastfeeding
risks.detail: Potential fetal harm. Highly effective contraception: women during treatment and ≥5 weeks afterwards; men with partners who could become pregnant during treatment and ≥3 months afterwards. Oral contraception may be less effective. Avoid breastfeeding and discuss fertility.

brigatinib.source_basis: NCCP 00562 v4 and current EMA Alunbrig SmPC retrieved 2026-10-29; independent clinical and pharmacy review remains pending. No numerical risk frequencies inferred.

risks.label: Early pulmonary reactions / pneumonitis
risks.detail: Severe or fatal lung inflammation can occur, particularly in the first week and also later. Report new cough or breathlessness immediately.

risks.label: Hypertension / bradycardia
risks.detail: High blood pressure and a slow heartbeat need monitoring; fainting, severe headache or chest symptoms need urgent assessment.

risks.label: Liver injury
risks.detail: Liver tests are monitored closely, especially in the first three months; serious liver injury can require stopping treatment.

risks.label: Hyperglycaemia and pancreatic enzyme elevations
risks.detail: Glucose and pancreatic enzymes can rise. Report unusual thirst, frequent urination or severe abdominal pain.

risks.label: CPK elevation / muscle symptoms
risks.detail: Raised CPK may occur with muscle pain or weakness; prompt reporting and blood tests guide treatment changes.

risks.label: Visual disturbance
risks.detail: New or worsening visual symptoms need assessment; severe changes can require stopping treatment.

risks.label: Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting and appetite change
risks.detail: Symptoms can impair hydration and tablet-taking; seek advice for severe or persistent problems.

risks.label: Rash / photosensitivity
risks.detail: Skin reactions and sun sensitivity can occur; use sun protection during treatment and for at least five days afterwards.

risks.label: Low blood counts / infection
risks.detail: Blood-count changes and infection can occur; report fever, shivering or sudden illness.

risks.label: Pregnancy, breastfeeding and fertility
risks.detail: Potential foetal harm and male fertility effects require discussion. Breastfeeding must stop during treatment; follow medicine-specific contraception advice.

lorlatinib.source_basis: Fresh NCCP 00570 v3 plus current EMA Lorviqua4.2–4.6; hepatic conflict and first-line NCCP source discrepancy require review. Checked 2026-10-29. No trial-derived frequency estimates borrowed.

risks.label: Cognitive, mood, speech and psychiatric effects
risks.detail: Changes in cognition, mood, mental status, speech or perceptions can require interruption, reduction or permanent stopping; severe changes need urgent assessment.

risks.label: Raised lipids and pancreatic inflammation
risks.detail: Cholesterol and triglycerides may rise without symptoms; blood tests and lipid treatment are important. Severe abdominal pain may signal pancreatitis.

risks.label: Heart conduction and heart-function problems
risks.detail: PR prolongation/AV block can cause dizziness or fainting; ECG monitoring and sometimes specialist cardiac treatment are needed. Reduced LVEF has been reported.

risks.label: Interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis
risks.detail: Lung inflammation can be severe or life-threatening; report new or worsening breathlessness and cough promptly.

risks.label: High blood pressure and high blood sugar
risks.detail: Monitoring and treatment may be needed; severe or uncontrolled effects can lead to interruption or stopping.

risks.label: Nerve symptoms, swelling, weight gain and fatigue
risks.detail: These can affect mobility, comfort and daily life; report functional changes.

risks.label: Bowel, sickness and skin effects
risks.detail: Diarrhoea, nausea and skin effects require review if persistent or troublesome.

risks.label: Pregnancy, fertility and contraception
risks.detail: Potential fetal harm, reduced reliability of hormonal contraception, possible male fertility effects and avoidance of breastfeeding require advance counselling.

crizotinib.source_basis: NCCP00243 v7 and current EMA Xalkori adult NSCLC SmPC/leaflet, checked 2026-10-29. Independent review remains pending. No paediatric risk frequencies or monitoring timetable imported.

sources.label: EMA Xalkori product information: adult NSCLC and patient leaflet

risks.label: Vision changes and severe visual loss
risks.detail: Report changes in vision; severe visual loss requires urgent ophthalmological assessment and treatment interruption during evaluation.

risks.label: Liver injury
risks.detail: Hepatotoxicity can be serious or fatal. Weekly early liver tests and urgent reporting of jaundice/dark urine are important.

risks.label: Interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis
risks.detail: New or worsening cough or breathlessness needs urgent assessment. Treatment-related lung inflammation can be serious or fatal.

risks.label: Slow pulse, QT prolongation and heart failure
risks.detail: Fainting, palpitations, breathlessness, oedema or rapid weight gain need prompt review. Medicines and electrolyte changes can increase risk.

risks.label: Kidney injury
risks.detail: Kidney function can worsen; report reduced urine or dehydration.

risks.label: Gastrointestinal perforation
risks.detail: Severe abdominal pain needs urgent assessment; bowel perforation has been reported.

risks.label: Low blood counts and infection
risks.detail: Neutropenia/leukopenia can occur. Fever, shivering or sudden illness needs prompt contact.

risks.label: Nausea, vomiting and bowel symptoms
risks.detail: A tailored prevention/rescue plan is needed for nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea or constipation; report poor intake and persistent symptoms.

risks.label: Swelling, fatigue, nerve and skin symptoms
risks.detail: Oedema, tiredness, neuropathy, rash and sun sensitivity can affect daily life; report changes and use sun protection.

risks.label: Pregnancy, breastfeeding and fertility
risks.detail: Potential fetal harm and impaired fertility. Discuss preservation; effective contraception during and ≥90 days after treatment; oral contraception may be less effective. Avoid breastfeeding during treatment.
